definitions.explanation: A grey, medium-sized songbird with brown cheeks, one of the commonest birds in Japanese towns and gardens. It has a loud, shrill call and feeds on fruit and on the nectar of flowers such as camellias.

examples.japanese: ヒヨドリ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}いている→鳴く：04388_naku⟧。

examples.english: A bulbul came to the camellia in the garden.

examples.japanese: ヒヨドリ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ピーヨ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}えなくて→見える：01165_mieru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦すぐ→すぐ：00814_sugu⟧⟦{分|わ}かる→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧。
examples.english: Bulbuls give a loud "pii-yo" call, so you know one is there even when you cannot see it.

notes:
USAGE:
A bird every Japanese city dweller knows by its noisy call, often seen pecking at garden fruit and vegetables. Gardeners count it as a pest.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The place name {鵯越|ひよどりごえ} near Kobe is famous for the cliff descent by Minamoto no Yoshitsune's cavalry at the battle of Ichi-no-Tani (1184), {鵯越|ひよどりごえ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{逆落|さかお}とし.

WRITING:
Written in katakana; the kanji {鵯|ひよどり} appears mainly in place names.
